info.title: Nuvora
info.description: The nuvora binary: config, HTTP API, OpenAPI document, embedded web app.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
An absolute folder. Absent: the filesystem roots (`/` on Unix, drive
letters on Windows).

delete.summary: Removes the library and its items from the catalog. Files on disk are untouched.

post.summary:
Scan now. Scans run over every library and coalesce, so this is the same
scan as `POST /api/scan`; the id must exist.

delete.summary: 409 `last_admin` for the last enabled admin; 400 for yourself.

patch.summary: 409 `last_admin` when the change would leave no enabled admin.

post.summary:
Sets the session cookie. Wrong username, wrong password and disabled
account all answer 401 `bad_credentials`. Each failure for a username makes
the next attempt wait (1 s, doubling, at most 10 s) and 20 failures from one
address within 15 minutes lock it for 15 minutes; until then the answer is
429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.
Ends this session and clears the cookie.

get.summary: Never 401: without a valid session `user` is `None`.

Direct play. Delegates to `tower_http::services::ServeFile` with the
container's MIME type, which implements `Range` (206 + `Content-Range`),
`If-Range`, `Last-Modified` and `HEAD`, and streams from disk without
buffering. First-frame latency is then disk + network + decoder.

Per user: cards carry the signed-in user's progress, and the ETag is
`"<catalog_rev>.<watch_rev>"`, so one user's progress never makes another
user's copy stale.

Reads the WebP from the store (tens of KB) and answers with
`Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` (private: it needs a
session, so a shared cache must not hand it to anyone else). Bad ids are 404, and
ids are parsed to 16 bytes before any path is built.

Per user: `watch` is the signed-in user's state. The ETag is
`"<catalog_rev>.<watch_rev>-<device profile hash>"`.

put.summary:
Reports where playback is; the server decides what it means. Under 60 s
stores nothing and clears earlier progress. From 60 s to under 90% of the
duration stores the position. From 90% the movie counts as watched once and
the position is cleared; another report at 90% or more within 3 hours of
that does not count again.
Marks the movie watched, like finishing it.

delete.summary:
Marks the movie unwatched: clears the position, the play count and the
last finish.

get.summary:
Keyset paging on the row's sort key. A malformed cursor, or one from
another row, is 400. Per user, with the same ETag as home.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: `next` from the previous page; absent = from the start.

get.summary: `issues` name server paths, so only admins see them.

post.summary: Idempotent: while a scan runs, repeated calls queue at most one more.

Creates the first admin and signs them in (sets the session cookie). 409
`setup_done` once any user exists.

item_count.description: Items with at least one file present.

missing_paths.description:
Entries of `paths` that cannot be read right now (unmounted share,
permissions). Their items stay in the catalog.

paths.description: Absolute folder paths on the server.

last_seen_at.description:
Unix ms of the latest request from any of the user's sessions;
`None` when the user has no session.

setup_required.description: True until the first admin exists. The web app then shows the welcome flow.

oneOf.description: The signed-in user, or `None` without a valid session.

CreateLibraryRequest.description:
`paths` are absolute folders that exist on the server; at least one, and
none already used by another library.

DeviceProfile.description:
What a device decodes natively. Sent as compact JSON in the `Nuvora-Device`
header. Codec and container names are the server's canonical names
(`h264`, `hevc`, `av1`, `vp9`; `aac`, `eac3`, `opus`; `mp4`, `mkv`, `webm`).
Unknown names are ignored, never errors, so old servers accept new clients.

ErrorBody.description:
Every API error answers with this body. `code` is stable; `message` is
written for people and may change.

field.description: The request field the error is about, for inline form validation.

ErrorCode.description: Clients must treat an unknown code like `bad_request`.

path.description: Absolute; pass it back as `?path=` to open the folder.

FsListing.description: One folder's subfolders. Files and hidden folders are never listed.

parent.description: The folder above `path`; `None` at a root.

path.description: The listed folder, canonical. Empty for the list of Windows drives.

rows.description: Render in order. Clients render unknown row kinds like any other row.

items.description: The first page, at most 40 cards.

next.description: Opaque cursor for `GET /api/rows/{row}?after=`. `None` when `items` is the whole row.

total.description: Cards in the whole row, not just `items`.

Image.description: An artwork. URL: `/api/images/{id}/{size}`. Immutable: cache forever.

aspect_ratio.description: width / height, for layout before the image loads.

placeholder.description: ThumbHash, base64. Decode client-side into a blurred placeholder.

ImageSize.description: Sizes a client can request. Pixel widths are a server decision.

versions.description: Best first. Empty when every file of the movie is currently missing.

reasons.description: Human-readable: `"HEVC video isn't supported on this device"`.

oneOf.description: The file could not be read (ffprobe failed); nothing will play it.

Playback.description:
What pressing Play does on the requesting device. Step 3 adds `hls`.
Clients must treat an unknown `kind` like `needs_transcode`.

progress.description:
How far the signed-in user is into the movie, 0 to 1. `None` unless
it is in progress.

watched.description: The signed-in user has finished the movie at least once.

ProgressRequest.description:
Where playback is. Clients send it every 10 s while playing, on pause,
after a seek settles and when leaving the player.

duration_ms.description: At least 1. `position_ms` may exceed it by at most 5 s.

file_id.description: The version playing. Must be a version of this item.

RowPage.description: A later page of one row.

issues.description: Files the scan could not read. Empty unless the signed-in user is an admin.

SetupRequest.description:
Creates the first admin. Usernames are 1 to 32 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or
`-`, unique ignoring case. Passwords are at least 8 characters.

version.description: As the tool reports it, e.g. `"7.1.1"`.

UpdateLibraryRequest.description:
Every field is optional. `paths` replaces the whole list; removing a folder
removes its items from the catalog (never from disk).

UpdateMeRequest.description:
Every field is optional. Changing the password needs both passwords, and
signs out the user's other sessions.

UpdateUserRequest.description:
Every field is optional. Disabling a user or resetting their password signs
them out everywhere. The last enabled admin cannot be demoted or disabled,
and nobody can disable themselves.

oneOf.description: `None` when the file could not be read.

summary.description:
One line for the version picker and detail header, built server-side so
every client says the same thing: `"4K · HEVC Main 10 · Dolby Vision · TrueHD 7.1"`.

WatchState.description: The signed-in user's state for one movie.

last_watched_at.description: Unix ms of the last finish.

position_ms.description: Where to resume. `None` unless the movie is in progress.
